_link.title: I can describe the two key properties of stem cells: self-renewal and potency

toLevel2.question: What are the two key properties of stem cells?

options.text: Self-renewal and potency
options.explanation: Stem cells are defined by their ability to self-renew (replicate) and their potency (ability to differentiate into specialised cell types).

options.text: Diffusion and osmosis
options.explanation: Diffusion and osmosis are transport processes, not properties of stem cells.

options.text: Mitosis and meiosis
options.explanation: Mitosis and meiosis are types of cell division, not the defining properties of stem cells.

options.text: Respiration and photosynthesis
options.explanation: These are metabolic processes, not defining properties of stem cells.

toLevel2.question: What does 'self-renewal' mean in the context of stem cells?

options.text: The ability to replicate and produce more of the same type of stem cell
options.explanation: Self-renewal means stem cells can divide to produce more stem cells, maintaining their own population.

options.text: The ability to differentiate into specialised cell types
options.explanation: Differentiating into specialised cells is potency, not self-renewal.

options.text: The ability to repair damaged DNA within the nucleus
options.explanation: DNA repair is a separate process; self-renewal is the replication of stem cells.

options.text: The ability to move to different parts of the body
options.explanation: Cell migration is not self-renewal; self-renewal is producing more stem cells.

toLevel2.question: What does 'potency' mean in the context of stem cells?

options.text: The ability to differentiate into specialised cell types
options.explanation: Potency refers to how many different cell types a stem cell can become through differentiation.

options.text: The ability to replicate and produce more stem cells
options.explanation: Producing more stem cells is self-renewal, not potency.

options.text: The strength of the cell membrane under pressure
options.explanation: Membrane strength is not related to potency; potency is about differentiation ability.

options.text: The speed at which a stem cell can divide
options.explanation: Division speed is not potency; potency is the range of cell types a stem cell can become.

toLevel2.question: Which cell type in bone marrow demonstrates both self-renewal and potency?

options.text: Haematopoietic stem cell
options.explanation: Haematopoietic stem cells self-renew and can differentiate into red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets.

options.text: Red blood cell
options.explanation: Red blood cells are fully specialised and cannot self-renew or differentiate further.

options.text: Platelet
options.explanation: Platelets are cell fragments produced from stem cells; they do not self-renew or differentiate.

options.text: Mature white blood cell
options.explanation: Mature white blood cells are specialised; haematopoietic stem cells produce them.

toLevel2.question: What types of blood cells can a haematopoietic stem cell differentiate into?

options.text: Red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets
options.explanation: Haematopoietic stem cells can produce all major blood cell types: red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets.

options.text: Muscle cells, nerve cells, and skin cells only
options.explanation: These are not blood cells; haematopoietic stem cells produce blood cell types.

options.text: Only red blood cells and no other cell types
options.explanation: Haematopoietic stem cells can produce multiple blood cell types, not just red blood cells.

options.text: Bone cells, cartilage cells, and fat cells only
options.explanation: These are produced by mesenchymal stem cells; haematopoietic stem cells produce blood cells.

toLevel2.question: Self-renewal is the ability of a stem cell to replicate and produce more of the same type of stem cell.

options.text: True
options.explanation: Correct. Self-renewal means stem cells can divide to produce more stem cells, maintaining their population.

options.text: False
options.explanation: This statement is true. Self-renewal is the replication of stem cells to maintain their numbers.

toLevel2.question: Potency is the ability of a stem cell to replicate itself.

options.text: True
options.explanation: Replicating itself is self-renewal. Potency is the ability to differentiate into specialised cell types.

options.text: False
options.explanation: Correct. Potency is the ability to differentiate into specialised cell types, not the ability to replicate.

toLevel2.question: The two key properties of stem cells are {{blank:1}} and {{blank:2}}.

options.text: self-renewal
options.explanation: Self-renewal is the ability to produce more of the same type of stem cell.

options.text: respiration
options.explanation: Respiration is a metabolic process, not a defining stem cell property.

options.text: osmosis
options.explanation: Osmosis is a transport process, not a stem cell property.

options.text: potency
options.explanation: Potency is the ability to differentiate into specialised cell types.

options.text: diffusion
options.explanation: Diffusion is a transport process, not a stem cell property.

options.text: mitosis
options.explanation: Mitosis is a type of cell division; potency is the differentiation ability of stem cells.

toLevel2.question: Self-renewal means a stem cell can {{blank:1}} to produce more {{blank:2}}.

options.text: replicate
options.explanation: Self-renewal involves replication (division) to produce more stem cells.

options.text: differentiate
options.explanation: Differentiation produces specialised cells, not more stem cells.

options.text: die
options.explanation: Cell death is not self-renewal; self-renewal involves replication.

options.text: stem cells
options.explanation: Self-renewal produces more of the same type of stem cell.

options.text: red blood cells
options.explanation: Producing red blood cells is differentiation (potency), not self-renewal.

options.text: muscle fibres
options.explanation: Producing muscle fibres is differentiation, not self-renewal.

toLevel2.question: Potency is the ability of a stem cell to {{blank:1}} into {{blank:2}} cell types.

options.text: differentiate
options.explanation: Potency refers to the ability to differentiate — to become specialised cell types.

options.text: self-renew
options.explanation: Self-renewal produces more stem cells; differentiation is the process described by potency.

options.text: divide
options.explanation: While division occurs, potency specifically refers to differentiation into specialised types.

options.text: specialised
options.explanation: Potency describes how many types of specialised cells a stem cell can produce.

options.text: identical
options.explanation: Producing identical cells is self-renewal; potency produces different specialised types.

options.text: dead
options.explanation: Stem cells differentiate into living specialised cells, not dead ones.

toLevel3.question: Why are both self-renewal and potency essential for stem cells to function effectively?

options.text: Self-renewal maintains the stem cell supply while potency produces the specialised cells needed
options.explanation: Without self-renewal, stem cells would be depleted. Without potency, they could not produce the specialised cells the body needs.

options.text: Self-renewal and potency serve the same function within the stem cell
options.explanation: They serve different functions: self-renewal maintains the population and potency produces specialised cells.

options.text: Only self-renewal is needed; potency is a minor secondary feature
options.explanation: Both are essential; without potency, stem cells could not produce the specialised cells the body requires.

options.text: Only potency is needed; self-renewal is not required for function
options.explanation: Without self-renewal, the stem cell population would be depleted and could not continue producing specialised cells.

toLevel3.question: How does a haematopoietic stem cell demonstrate both properties simultaneously?

options.text: It divides to make more stem cells and also differentiates into blood cell types
options.explanation: When it divides, some daughter cells remain as stem cells (self-renewal) while others differentiate into blood cells (potency).

options.text: It only produces red blood cells and cannot make more stem cells
options.explanation: It both self-renews and differentiates; it can produce more stem cells as well as blood cells.

options.text: It converts oxygen into glucose within the bone marrow environment
options.explanation: This describes metabolic processes, not the stem cell properties of self-renewal and potency.

options.text: It moves from bone marrow to the brain to create nerve cells
options.explanation: Haematopoietic stem cells produce blood cells, not nerve cells.

toLevel3.question: Why are stem cells considered valuable for medical therapies?

options.text: They can both replenish themselves and generate new specialised cells for repair
options.explanation: Their dual properties mean they can sustain themselves while producing replacement cells for damaged tissues.

options.text: They are more abundant than any other cell type in the body
options.explanation: Stem cells are relatively rare; their value comes from self-renewal and potency, not abundance.

options.text: They cannot differentiate and so remain stable for transplantation
options.explanation: Their ability to differentiate is exactly what makes them valuable for therapy.

options.text: They do not require any nutrients or energy to survive
options.explanation: All cells require nutrients; stem cells are valuable because of their unique properties.

toLevel3.question: What would happen if stem cells had potency but lacked self-renewal?

options.text: The stem cell supply would be depleted and could not be replenished
options.explanation: Without self-renewal, every division would produce only specialised cells, eventually exhausting the stem cell pool.

options.text: The stem cells would function normally with no consequences at all
options.explanation: Without self-renewal, the finite supply of stem cells would be used up.

options.text: More specialised cells would be produced faster than ever before
options.explanation: While specialised cells might initially be produced, the stem cell supply would deplete.

options.text: The cells would become cancerous and divide without any control
options.explanation: Cancer involves uncontrolled division; lacking self-renewal would lead to depletion, not cancer.

toLevel3.question: What would happen if stem cells had self-renewal but lacked potency?

options.text: They could replicate but not produce specialised cells the body needs
options.explanation: Without potency, stem cells would multiply but never differentiate, failing to produce the diverse cell types required.

options.text: They would immediately die without the potency property present
options.explanation: Cells can survive without differentiating; the problem would be an inability to produce specialised cells.

options.text: They would function identically to normal stem cells overall
options.explanation: Without potency, stem cells would be useless for producing the specialised cells the body needs.

options.text: They would differentiate into every possible cell type simultaneously
options.explanation: Lacking potency means they cannot differentiate at all, not that they differentiate into everything.

toLevel3.question: How do the properties of stem cells explain the body's ability to repair damaged tissue?

options.text: Self-renewal ensures a continuous supply while potency provides the replacement specialised cells
options.explanation: The body repairs tissue because stem cells maintain their population through self-renewal and produce replacement cells through differentiation.

options.text: Stem cells repair tissue by strengthening existing cells rather than replacing them
options.explanation: Stem cells produce new specialised cells to replace damaged ones; they do not strengthen existing cells.

options.text: Tissue repair occurs independently of stem cells through osmosis only
options.explanation: Tissue repair requires new cells from stem cells; osmosis is a transport process.

options.text: Stem cells are not involved in tissue repair at all in the body
options.explanation: Stem cells are central to tissue repair through self-renewal and differentiation.

toLevel3.question: Without self-renewal, the stem cell population would eventually be depleted because all cells would differentiate into specialised types.

options.text: True
options.explanation: Correct. Self-renewal prevents depletion by ensuring some daughter cells remain as stem cells.

options.text: False
options.explanation: This statement is true. Without self-renewal, every division would produce specialised cells, exhausting the stem cell pool.

toLevel3.question: Stem cells maintain their own {{blank:1}} through self-renewal while producing {{blank:2}} cells through potency.

options.text: population
options.explanation: Self-renewal maintains the population of stem cells so they are not depleted.

options.text: membrane
options.explanation: Self-renewal maintains the stem cell population, not the membrane.

options.text: energy
options.explanation: Self-renewal is about maintaining stem cell numbers, not energy production.

options.text: specialised
options.explanation: Potency allows stem cells to differentiate into specialised cell types.

options.text: identical
options.explanation: Producing identical stem cells is self-renewal; potency produces different specialised types.

options.text: cancerous
options.explanation: Potency produces normal specialised cells, not cancerous ones.

toLevel3.question: Stem cells are valuable for medicine because they can both {{blank:1}} themselves and {{blank:2}} new cells for repair.

options.text: replenish
options.explanation: Self-renewal allows stem cells to replenish their own numbers.

options.text: destroy
options.explanation: Stem cells replenish, not destroy, themselves through self-renewal.

options.text: eliminate
options.explanation: Self-renewal maintains stem cell numbers; elimination would deplete them.

options.text: generate
options.explanation: Through potency, stem cells generate new specialised cells needed for repair.

options.text: absorb
options.explanation: Stem cells generate new cells, not absorb existing ones.

options.text: dissolve
options.explanation: Stem cells produce new cells; they do not dissolve anything.

toLevel3.question: A haematopoietic stem cell demonstrates potency by differentiating into {{blank:1}}, {{blank:2}}, and platelets.

options.text: red blood cells
options.explanation: Haematopoietic stem cells can differentiate into red blood cells.

options.text: nerve cells
options.explanation: Haematopoietic stem cells produce blood cells, not nerve cells.

options.text: muscle cells
options.explanation: Haematopoietic stem cells produce blood cell types, not muscle cells.

options.text: white blood cells
options.explanation: Haematopoietic stem cells differentiate into white blood cells as part of their potency.

options.text: bone cells
options.explanation: Bone cells are produced by mesenchymal stem cells; haematopoietic stem cells make blood cells.

options.text: skin cells
options.explanation: Skin cells come from epithelial stem cells; haematopoietic stem cells produce blood cells.

toLevel4.question: A patient has a blood disorder that destroys their haematopoietic stem cells. Predict the consequences.

options.text: They would be unable to produce new red blood cells, white blood cells, or platelets
options.explanation: Without haematopoietic stem cells, the body loses both the self-renewing population and the potency to produce blood cells.

options.text: They would produce too many blood cells and need transfusions
options.explanation: Destroying stem cells would reduce blood cell production, not increase it.

options.text: Only red blood cells would be affected; white cells would be fine
options.explanation: Haematopoietic stem cells produce all blood cell types; losing them affects all types.

options.text: Their bones would weaken but blood production would continue
options.explanation: Blood production depends on haematopoietic stem cells; losing them stops blood cell formation.

toLevel4.question: A researcher isolates a cell that can divide to produce more of itself but cannot produce any other cell type. Does this cell qualify as a stem cell?

options.text: No; it has self-renewal but lacks potency
options.explanation: A stem cell requires both self-renewal and potency. Without the ability to differentiate, it does not meet the full definition.

options.text: Yes; self-renewal alone is sufficient to classify it as a stem cell
options.explanation: Both properties are required; self-renewal alone does not make a cell a stem cell.

options.text: Yes; potency is optional for stem cell classification in biology
options.explanation: Potency is a defining property of stem cells, not optional.

options.text: No; because it can divide, it must be a cancer cell instead
options.explanation: Division alone does not indicate cancer; the issue is that it lacks potency to be a stem cell.

toLevel4.question: In a bone marrow transplant, donor stem cells are introduced into a patient. Why must these transplanted cells have both self-renewal and potency?

options.text: Self-renewal sustains the transplant long-term; potency produces the needed blood cells
options.explanation: Without self-renewal, the transplanted cells would be depleted. Without potency, they could not produce the blood cells the patient needs.

options.text: Only potency is needed; the cells do not need to self-renew after transplant
options.explanation: Without self-renewal, the transplanted cells would eventually run out.

options.text: Only self-renewal matters; the body will differentiate cells on its own
options.explanation: The cells themselves must have potency to differentiate; the body does not force differentiation.

options.text: Neither property is needed because donor cells function differently
options.explanation: Donor stem cells function the same way and require both properties for successful transplantation.

toLevel4.question: A student observes skin healing after a cut. Which stem cell properties are demonstrated during this repair?

options.text: Self-renewal maintains the stem cell pool; potency produces new skin cells
options.explanation: Skin stem cells self-renew to maintain their numbers and differentiate to produce new skin cells that close the wound.

options.text: Only self-renewal; no new specialised cells are needed for healing
options.explanation: New specialised skin cells are required to repair the wound, demonstrating potency.

options.text: Only potency; stem cell numbers do not need maintaining during repair
options.explanation: Both properties are needed; self-renewal ensures stem cells remain available for future repair.

options.text: Neither property; skin repair occurs without stem cell involvement
options.explanation: Stem cells are essential for skin repair through both self-renewal and differentiation.

toLevel4.question: A scientist wants to develop a therapy using stem cells to treat a patient with liver damage. Which properties must the stem cells have?

options.text: Self-renewal to sustain treatment and potency to produce liver cells
options.explanation: The stem cells must self-renew to provide ongoing treatment and have the potency to differentiate into functional liver cells.

options.text: Only self-renewal; the liver will heal on its own once stem cells arrive
options.explanation: The stem cells must be able to differentiate into liver cells (potency), not just multiply.

options.text: Only potency; one round of differentiation is sufficient for full repair
options.explanation: Sustained repair requires self-renewal to maintain the stem cell supply over time.

options.text: Neither property; any cell type can repair liver damage equally
options.explanation: Specific stem cell properties are needed; not any cell can regenerate liver tissue.

toLevel4.question: After intense exercise, the body needs more red blood cells. Which stem cell property is primarily responsible for meeting this demand?

options.text: Potency, as stem cells differentiate into additional red blood cells
options.explanation: The demand for more red blood cells is met by haematopoietic stem cells differentiating (potency) into red blood cells.

options.text: Self-renewal, as stem cells simply divide to create red blood cells
options.explanation: Self-renewal produces more stem cells; potency (differentiation) produces the red blood cells needed.

options.text: Neither property; red blood cells are produced by the heart directly
options.explanation: Red blood cells are produced from haematopoietic stem cells in bone marrow, not by the heart.

options.text: Both are irrelevant; exercise does not affect blood cell production
options.explanation: Exercise increases oxygen demand, stimulating stem cell differentiation into more red blood cells.

toLevel4.question: A cell biologist discovers a new cell type that can differentiate into multiple specialised cells but cannot produce more of itself. What is this cell lacking?

options.text: Self-renewal
options.explanation: The cell has potency (can differentiate) but lacks self-renewal (cannot produce more of itself).

options.text: Potency
options.explanation: The cell can differentiate into multiple types, so it has potency; it lacks self-renewal.

options.text: Both self-renewal and potency
options.explanation: It has potency (can differentiate); it only lacks self-renewal.

options.text: Neither; it is a complete stem cell
options.explanation: Without self-renewal, it does not have both defining properties of a stem cell.

toLevel4.question: In a bone marrow transplant, {{blank:1}} ensures the transplanted cells last long-term, while {{blank:2}} allows them to produce the blood cells the patient needs.

options.text: self-renewal
options.explanation: Self-renewal maintains the transplanted stem cell population for ongoing blood cell production.

options.text: potency
options.explanation: Potency produces specialised cells; self-renewal is what sustains the transplant long-term.

options.text: osmosis
options.explanation: Osmosis is a transport process; self-renewal sustains the stem cell population.

options.text: potency
options.explanation: Potency allows the transplanted stem cells to differentiate into the required blood cell types.

options.text: self-renewal
options.explanation: Self-renewal maintains the population; potency produces the specialised blood cells.

options.text: diffusion
options.explanation: Diffusion is a transport process; potency is the property that produces blood cells.

toLevel4.question: A cell that can differentiate but cannot self-renew is {{blank:1}} a true stem cell because it lacks one of the two {{blank:2}} properties.

options.text: not
options.explanation: Without both self-renewal and potency, a cell does not meet the full definition of a stem cell.

options.text: definitely
options.explanation: A cell needs both properties; lacking self-renewal disqualifies it as a true stem cell.

options.text: always
options.explanation: Without self-renewal, the cell does not qualify as a stem cell.

options.text: defining
options.explanation: Self-renewal and potency are the two defining properties of stem cells.

options.text: optional
options.explanation: Both properties are defining, not optional; both are required.

options.text: metabolic
options.explanation: Self-renewal and potency are stem cell properties, not metabolic properties.

toLevel4.question: During wound healing, skin stem cells {{blank:1}} to maintain their numbers and {{blank:2}} into new skin cells to close the wound.

options.text: self-renew
options.explanation: Self-renewal maintains the stem cell population during and after wound repair.

options.text: differentiate
options.explanation: Differentiation produces specialised cells; maintaining numbers is self-renewal.

options.text: die
options.explanation: Stem cells do not die to maintain numbers; they self-renew.

options.text: differentiate
options.explanation: Differentiation (potency) produces the new specialised skin cells needed for wound closure.

options.text: self-renew
options.explanation: Self-renewal produces more stem cells; differentiation produces specialised skin cells.

options.text: dissolve
options.explanation: Stem cells do not dissolve; they differentiate into new skin cells.

toLevel5.question: Analyse why the balance between self-renewal and differentiation must be carefully regulated in stem cells.

options.text: Too much self-renewal could lead to tumour formation; too much differentiation depletes the stem cell pool
options.explanation: Uncontrolled self-renewal resembles cancer, while excessive differentiation exhausts the stem cell supply. Balance is essential for healthy tissue maintenance.

options.text: The balance does not matter because cells can switch between the two states freely
options.explanation: The balance is critical; dysregulation leads to disease (cancer or tissue failure).

options.text: Self-renewal should always dominate because more stem cells are always beneficial
options.explanation: Excessive self-renewal without differentiation resembles cancer; balance is essential.

options.text: Differentiation should always dominate to produce as many specialised cells as possible
options.explanation: Excessive differentiation would deplete the stem cell pool, preventing future repair.

toLevel5.question: Compare the consequences of losing self-renewal versus losing potency in haematopoietic stem cells.

options.text: Losing self-renewal depletes the stem cell pool; losing potency prevents blood cell production
options.explanation: Without self-renewal, stem cells run out. Without potency, they cannot produce the diverse blood cells needed. Both lead to different but serious consequences.

options.text: Both losses have identical consequences for the patient's health outcomes
options.explanation: The consequences differ: one depletes the source, the other prevents the product.

options.text: Losing self-renewal is beneficial because it prevents cancer from forming
options.explanation: While uncontrolled self-renewal can be problematic, losing it entirely would be fatal as stem cells deplete.

options.text: Losing potency has no effect because other cells compensate fully
options.explanation: Other cells cannot compensate for the loss of blood cell production from stem cells.

toLevel5.question: Evaluate the statement: 'Self-renewal is more important than potency for stem cell function.'

options.text: Neither is more important; both are equally essential and interdependent
options.explanation: Self-renewal without potency produces useless cells. Potency without self-renewal eventually runs out. Both are equally necessary.

options.text: Correct; self-renewal is clearly more important for all applications
options.explanation: Without potency, self-renewal alone produces stem cells that cannot contribute specialised cells to the body.

options.text: Correct; potency can be acquired later through genetic modification
options.explanation: Potency is a fundamental property, not easily acquired; both properties are equally essential.

options.text: Potency is more important because differentiation is the primary purpose
options.explanation: Without self-renewal, the stem cell supply depletes; both properties are equally essential.

toLevel5.question: A student argues: 'All dividing cells are stem cells because they can self-renew.' Evaluate this claim.

options.text: Incorrect; stem cells also require potency — the ability to produce different specialised cell types
options.explanation: Many cells can divide (e.g., liver cells, skin cells) but only stem cells have both self-renewal and the potency to differentiate into different cell types.

options.text: Correct; any cell that divides qualifies as a stem cell by definition
options.explanation: Division alone is not sufficient; stem cells must also have potency (differentiation ability).

options.text: Correct; self-renewal is the only defining property of all stem cells
options.explanation: Stem cells have two defining properties: self-renewal and potency.

options.text: Incorrect; stem cells never divide and only differentiate into new types
options.explanation: Stem cells do divide (self-renewal); the error is that not all dividing cells are stem cells.

toLevel5.question: Analyse how the dual properties of stem cells make them uniquely suited for long-term tissue maintenance compared to fully differentiated cells.

options.text: Differentiated cells cannot replace themselves or produce other cell types; stem cells can do both
options.explanation: Fully differentiated cells are specialised for function but cannot self-renew or produce other types. Stem cells uniquely provide both functions.

options.text: Differentiated cells and stem cells have identical capabilities for tissue repair
options.explanation: Differentiated cells lack self-renewal and potency; they cannot contribute to long-term tissue maintenance the way stem cells can.

options.text: Stem cells are inferior to differentiated cells for tissue maintenance
options.explanation: Stem cells are essential for ongoing tissue maintenance because differentiated cells cannot replace themselves.

options.text: Differentiated cells can self-renew but not differentiate further into types
options.explanation: Most differentiated cells cannot self-renew; they are replaced by stem cell differentiation.

toLevel5.question: Evaluate why stem cell therapies are considered promising for treating degenerative diseases like Parkinson's disease.

options.text: Stem cells could self-renew to sustain treatment and differentiate into replacement neurons
options.explanation: In Parkinson's, dopamine-producing neurons die. Stem cells could potentially provide a renewable source of replacement neurons through potency.

options.text: Stem cells cure all diseases instantly without any need for further treatment
options.explanation: Stem cell therapies are promising but complex; they do not instantly cure all diseases.

options.text: Stem cells are only useful for blood disorders and have no other applications
options.explanation: Stem cells have potential applications across many tissue types, not just blood.

options.text: Stem cell therapies are impossible because stem cells cannot differentiate at all
options.explanation: Differentiation (potency) is a defining property of stem cells and is the basis of their therapeutic potential.

toLevel5.question: Consider a scenario where a stem cell divides: one daughter cell remains a stem cell and the other becomes a red blood cell. Analyse which properties are demonstrated by each daughter cell.

options.text: The stem cell daughter demonstrates self-renewal; the red blood cell daughter demonstrates potency
options.explanation: Self-renewal is shown by the daughter that remains a stem cell. Potency is shown by the daughter that differentiates into a red blood cell.

options.text: Both daughters demonstrate self-renewal because both came from division
options.explanation: Only the daughter remaining as a stem cell shows self-renewal; the other shows potency through differentiation.

options.text: Both daughters demonstrate potency because both are new cell types
options.explanation: The stem cell daughter shows self-renewal; only the differentiating daughter demonstrates potency.

options.text: Neither daughter demonstrates any stem cell property at all
options.explanation: One demonstrates self-renewal and the other demonstrates potency; both properties are shown.

toLevel5.question: A textbook defines stem cells as 'undifferentiated cells with the ability to become specialised.' A student argues this definition is incomplete. Evaluate their argument.

options.text: Valid; the definition omits self-renewal, which is equally important as a defining property
options.explanation: The textbook definition only covers potency. A complete definition must include self-renewal as the second defining property.

options.text: Invalid; the textbook definition is complete and covers all properties
options.explanation: The definition is incomplete; it only describes potency and omits self-renewal.

options.text: Valid; but only because it should mention the cell cycle instead
options.explanation: The missing element is self-renewal specifically, not just the cell cycle in general.

options.text: Invalid; self-renewal is not a property that needs to be mentioned
options.explanation: Self-renewal is a defining property of stem cells and should be included in any complete definition.

toLevel5.question: When a stem cell divides asymmetrically, one daughter cell {{blank:1}} (demonstrating self-renewal) and the other {{blank:2}} (demonstrating potency).

options.text: remains a stem cell
options.explanation: The daughter that stays as a stem cell demonstrates self-renewal.

options.text: becomes specialised
options.explanation: Becoming specialised demonstrates potency, not self-renewal.

options.text: undergoes apoptosis
options.explanation: Apoptosis is programmed cell death; the self-renewing daughter remains a stem cell.

options.text: differentiates
options.explanation: The daughter that becomes a specialised cell demonstrates potency through differentiation.

options.text: remains a stem cell
options.explanation: Remaining as a stem cell is self-renewal; differentiation demonstrates potency.

options.text: dissolves
options.explanation: Cells do not dissolve during division; the daughter differentiates into a specialised type.

toLevel5.question: Excessive self-renewal without differentiation can lead to {{blank:1}}, while excessive differentiation without self-renewal would {{blank:2}} the stem cell pool.

options.text: tumour formation
options.explanation: Uncontrolled self-renewal without differentiation resembles cancer, leading to tumour growth.

options.text: tissue repair
options.explanation: Tissue repair requires balanced self-renewal and differentiation, not excessive self-renewal.

options.text: cell shrinkage
options.explanation: Excessive self-renewal leads to cell accumulation (tumours), not shrinkage.

options.text: deplete
options.explanation: Without self-renewal, all stem cells would differentiate and the pool would be exhausted.

options.text: expand
options.explanation: Differentiation reduces, not expands, the stem cell pool.

options.text: stabilise
options.explanation: Excessive differentiation without self-renewal would deplete, not stabilise, the stem cell population.
